title: Fab City Index 3.0 — submission row
description: One row per observation. Raw values only; the dashboard normalises.

cell.description: Which of the twenty parts of city life this belongs to. Pillar and scale, separated by a colon.

indicator.description: Exactly what was counted. Use the indicator name listed in the cell.

value.description: The raw number as measured. Do not pre-convert it to 0–1 — the platform normalises.

unit.description: The unit the number is in. Without this the value cannot be normalised or compared.

observation_date.description: When the measurement refers to (not when you typed it). ISO format, YYYY-MM-DD.

source.description: Where it came from, specific enough that somebody else could go and check.

scale_min.description: The bottom of the range you are scaling against — the raw value that would count as 0. State it so your normalisation is auditable.

scale_max.description: The top of that range — the raw value that would count as 1. A practical ceiling, a peer benchmark, or a science-based target.

team.description: Who submitted this. Used to attribute the reading back to your table.

method.description: How it was collected. Optional, but this is what makes the number auditable a year from now.
examples: Manual count at close of each session

geography.description: The exact area the number covers, if narrower than the cell's scale.

confidence.description: Your own honest read: high, medium, or low. Low-confidence rows go to review rather than committing.

notes.description: Anything a reader would need to know to not misread the number.
examples: Two sessions cancelled in June; undercount likely
